newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt promises infrastructure fund.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt promises infrastructure fund.

text.p: The Australian government, battling to gain the votes of two crucial Independent senators, promised to create a A$250 million fund to develop regional telecoms infrastructure if the Senate approved its plan to sell a third of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp.
Communications Minister Richard Alston also said that the government had sweetened its environmental package, adding A$100 million to the A$1 billion fund already promised.
Tasmania, the home state of one of the Independents, would get priority, he told the Senate.

"Accordingly, the government is prepared to commit A$250 million from the proceeds of the potential sale of Telstra to create a regional telecommunications infrastructure fund which will operate over five years," Alston said.
"The money will be used to improve the quality of telecommunications services and to enhance employment opportunities in regional areas throughout Australia."
One Independent, Brian Harradine, is from Tasmania.
The other, Mal Colston, is from Queensland and has said his vote hinges on his concerns for the effect of the sale on employment outside of main cities.

Alston said the conservative Liberal-National government had reassessed the level of damage to the Australian environment, which is supposed to be met by a repair fund to be established from the estimated A$8 billion proceeds of the sale.
"We have decided to increase the contribution to the fund by another A$100 million, so the capital contribution from the sale to the environment would be A$1.1 billion," the minister said.
The government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate, but all non-government senators except the Independents have declared their opposition to the privatisation.
